newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel rises against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel rises against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel's representative rate was fixed higher against the dollar but declined against the basket of key foreign currencies on Thursday in active trading, dealers said.
"The shekel rose today against the dollar as the business sector converted dollars for mid-month tax payments," said a dealer at United Mizrahi Bank.

She added that the shekel-dollar rate was also reacting to the dollar's slide in Europe. "Today we saw that investors continue to repay yen- and mark-linked loans which led to another rise of the basket," the dealer said.
Many Israeli companies turned to foreign currency loans in the last two years because of high domestic interest rates.

Dealers noted that activity was relatively high, adding that the market was not affected by forecasts of a relatively high April consumer price index (CPI) of 1.1-1.2 percent. The CPI will be released later on Thursday.

"If the CPI is higher than one percent, the Bank of Israel will leave its key lending rate unchanged. A lower than expected CPI might lead to a rate cut that will eventually affect also the forex trade," the Mizrahi dealer said.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3920 shekels against 3.3990 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.7020 shekels against 3.6942 on Wednesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.9371 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.8639 on Wednesday, and against the mark at 2.0075 shekels compared with 1.9913 on Wednesday.
In the late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.3945 shekels.
